scope: Retrospective reconstructed three-hour Manhattan station departures pilot; independent of the live aggregate model
cohort: Up to 32 Manhattan stations, lexically sorted by string short_name, with unique UUID/short_name and stable coordinates in April 6/7 information snapshots. No outcome-based selection.
label_availability: max(target month end +45 days 00 UTC, every supplying source cohort month end +45 days 00 UTC); strict before fit cutoff
validation_selection_availability: Every validation target label must be mature before September fit cutoff; do not use July spillovers that mature September 14
boundary_purge: All three targets must remain inside the specified target partition
operation_population: Hours fully bracketed by observed installed/renting status with provider age <=120 seconds and station report age between -300 and 600 seconds, consecutive polls at most 120 seconds apart, stable identity/coordinates, and complete ledger-selected trip inputs. Bounded interpolation assumption; no proof of uninterrupted operation between polls. Empty inventory remains eligible.
metadata_availability: Use previous UTC day's information only after that day ends plus 1 hour, with provider timestamp before cutoff. Exact historical retrieval not retained: this is a declared conservative scenario, not verified first publication. Reject moves >25m and duplicate/missing identifiers.
geography: Dated information snapshots matched to versioned MTA GTFS parent stops; archive version must predate cutoff. Radius 500m primary, 250m descriptive sensitivity only.
weather: Existing Manhattan ECMWF IFS point proxy; initialization +7h strict before origin cutoff; no actual-weather replacement
alerts: Latest archived full snapshot fetched strictly before cutoff; provider age -300..900sec. Preserve full active_periods_json, AND selector restrictions, OR selectors, deduplicate entity per station. Reject unsupported trip restrictions. Missing/stale snapshot is missing, not zero advisories.
selection: Choose alpha separately per family by June common-key validation MAE, persist selections before September metrics, refit selected families on individually mature April-June common-key examples before September cutoff
primary_metric: MAE on identical station/origin/horizon keys with supported label operation and fresh weather/advisory inputs
limitations: Reconstructed retrospective evaluation, not forecasts actually issued in 2026
September aggregate outcomes were inspected previously; station outcomes/ablation not yet evaluated
Assumed trip-release, weather and information availability
Observed polling supports a conditional operating-hour population
Small metadata-selected cohort and one geography/weather proxy
Matched advisories do not establish actual disruption or causal effect
